utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Tieger, the Chamber was informed that there was a preliminary matter you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, a very brief one. At the beginning of yesterday's court day, the Chamber inquired about the Prosecution's position in relation to a motion for videolink filed by the Defence on September 30th. I can advise the Court -- and I should also mention that the Chamber invited the Prosecution to provide an expedited response. Accordingly, I can advise the Chamber that the Prosecution does not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I again remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Continuing with the incident on 22nd December 1994, I would like to discuss the origin of fire with you now. In your report at paragraph 101, you acknowledge that: "Police determined that the rounds had come in from a direction 159 degrees in relation to the north. UNMO observers obtained a similar result. They determined that the incoming direction was 160 degrees." This direction would be to the south, slightly to the east, toward the area of Vidikovac and Trebevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, just for a correction, the transcript -- oh, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But Ms. Subotic didn't hear the correction. Because we did receive the translation as it was entered the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll just reread the question then. I don't know what was heard and not heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report at paragraph 101, you acknowledge that: "Police determined that the rounds had come in from a direction 159 degrees in relation to the north. UNMO observers obtained a similar result. They determined that the incoming direction was 160 degrees." This direction would be to the south, slightly to the east, toward the area of Vidikovac and Trebevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You reviewed the Bosnian MUP investigative file and relied on a few statements from this file; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We read all the statements that existed there. We relied on those that we cited, and I believe we made references to all the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You agree that the sound of a mortar or artillery piece being fired can give an indication of the direction of fire; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: An artillery shell --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: An artillery shell, due to its rotation in the air, produces a whizzing sound; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar shells produce that sound because they fly in a subsonic field. Artillery shells don't. But it all depends on their initial velocity. We distinguish between the mortar programme and the artillery programme. That's why I'm answering the way I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D01259. It's presently under seal so we ask that it not be broadcast. If we could please go to page 5 of the B/C/S and page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, this is the 22nd December 1994 official report on the incident. Directing your attention to the last paragraph on the page before you where the report discusses the forensic investigation and reads -- this is in the middle of the page in the English: "Judging by the incoming descent angle of the shells and the damage they inflicted, it was established that the shells had been fired from the south at Trebevic where the aggressor forces are located. The shell fragments indicated that they were fired from a B1, 76-millimetre calibre cannon." These were the kinds of shell fragments recovered during this incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 76. Yes, of course. But I have one correction to make. I heard in the interpretation 82 millimetres. I can't see whether it's really written here, but it's probably 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think we're clear on the type of shell fragments. Could the Prosecution please have page 11 of the B/C/S and page 6 of the English translation. I'm just going to go through these two documents from the file quickly. This is a 24 December 1994 Official Note of an interview with an individual who stated that he heard the sound of two successive shells being fired from the plateau on Vidikovac from about 500 metres away from his house, followed by explosions near the flea market by the Vijecnica building, and he saw the smoke. And he indicated -- and saw -- smoke in that area. If we could go to one more. If we could have the next page in both versions. This is another Official Note dated two days later from a different individual who indicated that at about 0900 he heard the sound of artillery projectiles firing from the direction of the plateau on Vidikovac, and a few seconds later, he heard loud explosions from the direction of Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The fact is that multiple witnesses heard the rounds being fired on the 22nd of December, 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we are talking about two occurrences. I said that the flight of artillery projectiles is not heard; whereas the flight of mortar projectiles --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you're not --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is heard because of the subsonic area --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You're talking about something that I didn't ask. I'm talking about the sound of the rounds being fired, not their flight. Could you please answer my question. The fact is that multiple witnesses heard the rounds being fired on the 22nd of December, 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see the document here now, but in any case, I don't read anywhere that they heard both the firing and the explosion. The copy is rather bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, perhaps you read the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The sound of firing of an artillery projectile -- yes, it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. This witness certainly did state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to look at your analysis of witness W-12's testimony from the Dragomir Milosevic case on the origin of fire for this incident. At the end of paragraph 95 of your report, you state: "Witness W-12 could not determine objectively whether the sound had come from the direction of Vidikovac where the VRS positions were or from the area of Colina Kapa where the BH army's 115th Brigade had its positions because the two positions were very close."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33163, page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to be referring you to line 17. This is W-12's open session testimony. The witness was asked: "Q. Thank you. How did you establish -- I mean, based on your knowledge and experience, how did you reach the conclusion that the shell you heard was fired from Vidikovac?" W-12 answered: "Well, because our positions were much lower. The highest position was at Colina Kapa, and the sound of its being fired was coming from the left and from a higher elevation, that is to say, from the direction of Vidikovac. "Q. So based on what you heard and what you observed that day, you were able to reach the conclusion that the shell was fired from Vidikovac?" Next page, please. W-12's answer: "Yes. "Q. Isn't Vidikovac a part of Mount Trebevic? "A. Yes, it is." This is the testimony that you reviewed for your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not accurately characterise the observations of this witness in your report. He was quite clear as to why he was able to observe the firing from the direction he heard; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, he did not say that he saw it. He explained why he was able to hear. Second, he said in his statement that he heard the firing and then the explosion. But then further below in his statement, he stated that it was only from his own home that he heard about the second explosion, and we know that both explosions in Bascarsija happened within an interval of a couple of seconds. And, finally, in figure 90 it is very clearly shown, I believe even he marked it himself, which of these positions were where when he heard the sound of one firing and one explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 12130 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, ma'am, I'm not further discussing it with you, but just so you know that our position is that you've combined -- it sounds like you possibly combined information from multiple individuals from the file in your last answer. This is a 4 October 1993 SRK Command order. Under item 1, General Milosevic re-subordinates one anti-aircraft gun to the VP, meaning firing position, Vidikovac. Do you accept that the VRS held firing positions in Vidikovac in the fall of 1993? Or during the war, I should rephrase.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this order, one could say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This Chamber has received evidence that the VRS possessed 14 B1 76-millimetre cannons around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I'd refer the Chamber to Exhibit P4496, page 2, item 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you accept the fact that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps possessed this type of cannon?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason not to accept that, but that has no specific relation to the specific incident because it's not linked to anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So you're saying as part of your consideration of this event that you didn't even consider whether or not the VRS had a firing position in the area that is indicated in the file or whether or not the VRS possessed the type of weapon that the shell fragments were -- were consistent with? You didn't even consider those things?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, both the VRS and the BH army had the same weapons at their disposal, so I don't see why I would link the possession of a weapon with a particular incident. I analysed the traces at the site of the incident, and on that basis, I made my conclusions in keeping with the rules of science and the profession, whereas both sides had identical weapons at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. So you didn't consider the fact that the ABiH 1st Corps had only one B1 cannon and it was located very far outside Sarajevo, outside the -- what the SRK referred to as the external ring. You didn't consider that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I don't see why that should be taken into account --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- especially if the cannon B1 is movable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not why but the question is whether you did consider the fact which Mr. Weber put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We took it into account. It's not a problem. The possession of only one weapon allows for the possibility that it was fired. We just did not believe that it had anything to do with the result on the location. Who would now be able to tell us where that cannon was on that day? That one cannon. And who can claim that there were not more of them? I'm just saying that both sides had the same weapons, and that's not a parameter for making this kind of analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to you, Ms. Subotic. You just said: "We took it into account." Four lines before that, you said: "I repeat, I don't see why that should be taken into account ..." You had no reason to take it into account but you did, or how do I have to understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very simple to understand. We knew that both sides had both kinds of weapon, and we did not analyse from that point of view. Because we analyse an incident on the spot where the projectile impacted, based on the traces collected on site and based on traces left by the impact. That's how you determine weapons, projectiles, and, if possible, the incoming trajectory and the distance. I hope this answers your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. The question was: Why you first said: I didn't see why that should be taken into account. Then the Presiding Judge urged you to answer that question. And then you said: "We took it into account." It's just the contrary. I would like to have an explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We took it into account. In principle, this relates to the fact that we knew both sides had that weapon in their possession. That's the sense in which we took it into account, not from whose cannon it was fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that you allow for the possibility that it was fired from the VRS side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot allow for the possibility that it was fired either from the VRS cannon nor from the BiH army cannon because the traces on the ground indicate something else. It's technically impossible for a cannon, no matter whose, to fire two projectiles within a couple of seconds' interval and create such different craters as we found on the market on 22nd December 1994. These craters are completely different in appearance, and they would have to arrive from the same angle, the same tube, and in the same spot. They should have created very similar craters because there is no such mechanical action that would allow for one crater to be very shallow and the other one very deep. It is technically impossible because these projectiles would have had to be fired under the same angle, and since they were fired from one tube - if they were - then the craters cannot be so different. We explained that in detail in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a -- if it is not what it was said to be, what is your conclusion as to -- not to what it was not but what it may have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't quite understand the question. If it is not what it is said to be? Who was saying this? Is it I or is it the Bosnian investigators? I didn't quite understand the question. Perhaps there is imprecision in the interpretation that I received. But please understand that I have to understand what I'm being asked in order to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say it couldn't have been a 76-millimetre cannon. What in your option would it possibly have been if not a 76-millimetre cannon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We fully analysed the traces very carefully. I mean, in accordance with our profession and science, and we came to the conclusion that these are unrelated explosions. That there's one, and it's in the photo documentation. Let me not make a mistake here. The one that is marked as number 2 on the sketch of the scene. In our view, and according to the technical characteristics involved, it was created due to an explosive that was not enclosed in casing. And the second one, marked with number 1 on the sketch, that - most probably - was created through the static activation of a projectile that was horizontal. That is indicated by the size of the crater. It is shallow and wide. And also the fuse that was found on the spot. Statically activated in a horizontal position. Most probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So both shells or at least the explosives which exploded at the time were put in place and then activated and then exploded. They did not fly into their position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That is indicated by all the traces found on the spot itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have some -- a few questions too. Ma'am, at page 10, starting from line 15, are you recorded as having said the following: "I cannot allow for the possibility that it was fired either from the VRS cannon or from the ABiH army cannon because the traces on the ground indicate something else. It's technically impossible for a cannon, no matter whose, to fire two projectiles within a couple of seconds' interval and create such different craters as we found on the market on the 22nd of December, 1994." My question to you is: Do I understand you correctly to be saying because the craters were different, you can therefore not make -- cannot allow for the possibility that it either came from the VRS or from an ABiH cannon? Is that your reasoning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is my reasoning. But it's not my only reasoning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. Now, are you able to postulate a third source from which it could have come if it didn't come from either of these two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, hypothetically I cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking hypothetically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm asking factually. Your investigation clearly says it could never be either of the two because the craters are different. I'm saying what was the source, then, according to your analysis? Practically not hypothetically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Practically the only possible technical explanation is that at location number 2, that is, in this street called Oprkanj, I think that's what is written here. So the place of the incident where an explosion occurred, marked with the number 2, at that place it is only possible that an explosive exploded, TNT or something like that, that was placed there. As for location number 1, most probably it probably exploded -- a projectile of 76 millimetres or 70 millimetres statically activated in a horizontal position. That is the only thing that would fit into the situation on the ground according to the photo documentation that was supplied and the effects that we can see, on the basis of this photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So, according to your analysis, both these explosions were detonated statically. They didn't fly over. That's your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, one was probably a projectile and the other one was just an explosive that was freely placed there. And they did not fly in, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, in this discussion of your theory of what happened here, the fact is you're ignoring what multiple witnesses said, the physical traces of 76-millimetre projectiles, and facts in the investigative file. In order to come to your conclusion, you're ignoring the evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. You're absolutely not right. And I tried to remember all the things that you listed in order. There are different statements but, say, the statement of the witness that you mentioned, W-12, precisely indicates this fact, that I'm speaking of. Actually, he heard an explosion of lesser intensity and then -- actually he identified that as a firing sound. And then he came home, and then he heard of another explosion that he hadn't even known about. Had he been there, he would have to hear two firings and two explosions. If he was there at that place. I'm not doubting that he was there, but I'm saying that from that place, he would have to hear two firings and two explosions in succession. He heard one firing, one explosion. That's what you said. That is the first point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, first of all --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secondly, it is not true that if something was not analysed --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First of all -- you're going on, but that's not what I said. And I would put it to you, actually, that W-12 heard two shots. I don't want to engage in a long debate with you about it. We have his statement in the investigative file where the witness indicates two firings. So I was just putting a question to you. Do you have anything else that you want to add?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe Ms. Subotic should answer first and then I will say what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I saw you were on your feet. That's the reason why I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Prosecutor interrupted me. He told me that I hadn't taken into account the material evidence that was collected, shrapnel. On the contrary, I did take that into account. And that is also a plus factor in terms of making such a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what Mr. Weber did put to you is that Witness W-12 stated that he heard two firings; whereas your answer is based on the fact that he would have said that he heard only one firing sound. And I think it's that matter which Mr. Weber asked you to comment about, if you have any comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he said that he heard two shots of different intensity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in page 14, line 22, it was entered and probably translated: "That's what you said." And actually Ms. Subotic said: "That's what you missed." So that's why there was confusion on Mr. Weber's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I appreciate that, and I'm sorry I -- and it appears like that's now been resolved even with the understanding of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the present document into evidence. It is 65 ter 12130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 12130 receives Exhibit Number P7558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before the break I'd like to turn and discuss with you the two shelling incidents on Livanjska Street on 8 November 1994. Regarding the first shelling incident where one shell landed at 1525 hours, the BiH MUP investigators and the UNPROFOR investigators concluded that the shell had come from the direction of north-west of Livanjska Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Both BiH MUP and UNPROFOR reports for that first shelling conclude that the shell originated from SRK-held territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not quite clear, Mr. Weber. It could be understand as whether the witness agrees with that finding or whether she agrees that that was reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking her that's what they reported. If I can make it more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the reports of both BiH MUP and UNPROFOR, the shell originated from SRK territory; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. This was after a serious disagreement in terms of the findings of UNPROFOR and the Bosnian police. I mean, this was harmonised, this report, because the Bosnian police opposed the initial position taken by UNPROFOR; namely that the critical shell had been fired from BH territory. If we all remember from a couple of days ago, this was the discussion about the alleged --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you've answer -- let's go through it step by step. I want to go to your conclusion. You conclude, though, at the end of paragraph 156A, that the shell, and I'm referring to the shelling at 1525, was not launched from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska on the basis, as I understand it, of an assertion that the police determined that the shell had been fired from 2475 metres away from the location of impact. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When I was looking then at paragraph 142 of your report, it appears that the police came to this determination, according to you, on the basis of a sketch of a mortar. Is this your source for where you get the measurement from? Of 2475 metres.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I heard an interpretation that is wrong. I'm sure that you didn't say that. You said that I based that on a sketch of a mortar. That makes no sense, and I'm quite certain that you said something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I called it a sketch, but a diagram of a mortar where they did a calculation where there was then a measurement of 2475. That's where you're getting this from; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that what you were trying to say is that this was taken from 126, that was compiled by the team of the Bosnian investigators, and they determined the angle of descent and the distance on that basis from which this shell was fired in order to be able to fall at that angle. So it's not mortar, it's shell. I understand that there is lack of clarity in the translation and that all of it is not clear to you. So, yes, if that's what you were trying to ask, that is that. That was all taken from this material, and 470 is the reference used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's be clear about what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33104, page 13 of the B/C/S and page 11 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is the investigative file for the -- what I have been calling the first shelling and where the one shell landed at 1525 hours on the 8th. This is the diagram that you referred to in your report where you then get the measurement which we see in the lower right-hand corner of 2475 metres and then, in the parentheses, what you have associated to be a determination of 0 plus 3 charges; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not the one who linked that up. They are the ones who wrote that. They wrote that the projectile arrived from 0 plus 3 and that that is the distance on the basis of the angle of descent. You just confused me when you said this was a sketch of a mortar. It was the sketch of a shell. Sorry. That's why this debate has been going on unnecessarily for a while now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I think it was asked whether you drew your conclusions on the basis of what we've seen on the screen. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the information that we used for our analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then perhaps next time you just say: Yes, that's the basis on which I drew my conclusions, instead of commenting on all kind of other matters, including that the debate is unnecessarily going for a while now. That's -- there's no need to hear that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What we see before us calculates the angle of descent and mentions what is the minimum distance if the mortar was fired on 0 plus 3 charges; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over here on the sketch, there is a distance. I would have to check whether that is the minimum distance on 0 plus 3, but then there are other technical reasons involved. It's not that somebody is just saying that it's the minimum distance. Because, I mean, well, there are reasons related to how the stabiliser was stuck there. So had it been 5 or 6, charge 5 or 6, it would have completely been stuck into the surface, the crater would not be 3 centimetres deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We've covered that one already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page, we see another diagram from the file calculating the possible ranges for the same angle of descent for charges 3, 4, 5 and 6. On the next page of this file, we see that the investigators determined that the mortar could have been fired up to 4350 metres. The fact is that the investigators considered all of the possible charges upon which this mortar could have been fired, all the way up to charge 6; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They certainly provided - and that's a good thing - all the distances that can be involved with this angle of descent. However, the situation on the terrain does not valuate charges 4 to 6. I already mentioned that because of the situation on the ground. I said that a moment ago. If it were charge 6, then the stabiliser would be fully stuck into the ground. 5, too. 4 considerably more than these 3 centimetres. And that is why it was analysed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the investigative file into evidence, 65 ter 33104. And then we'd actually ask to admit two photo files; one photo file relates to the earlier shelling at 1525, and the second photo file relates to the later shelling at 1725. The investigative file for the second shelling is in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33104 receives Exhibit Number P7559, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Then the photo file for the shelling at 1525 hours is 65 ter 33235.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives Exhibit Number P7560.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The photo file for the second shelling at 1725 hours is 65 ter 18645.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives Exhibit Number P7561, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was going to start in on a new matter. If this is an acceptable time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then take the break first. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning to Markale I on 5 February 1994, in your Markale report, 1D5496, you discuss this incident between paragraphs 1 and 78. What I'd like to do today is first discuss some general matters related to the report, and then we'll more specifically focus and discuss your theory as to what happened. In paragraphs 8 to 34 of your Markale report, you discuss what is seen in the videos related to the incident and provide numerous observations and various personal opinions about what is depicted ranging from the stalls, to the injuries sustained by the victims of the explosion. At the end of paragraph 34 of your report, you state: "We stress that a similar scene was also recorded during the evacuation of the casualties in Vase Miskina Street on 27 May 1992." The Vase Miskina Street evacuation and casualties were the result of a mortar explosion; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you acknowledge that the injuries to the individuals at the market-place on 5 February 1994 were also caused by mortar shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have watched the videos related to both the Markale 1 and Markale II events. In both instances, you can see in the videos that the scenes were chaotic, and there were many people and vehicles moving around; correct? In the aftermath of the explosions I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraphs 35 to 45 of your Markale report, you discuss the casualties and the number of victims. As we've just discussed, you've seen the videos relating to the immediate aftermath of the explosion. In that video, there's what appears to be a great deal of blood. Do you feel that all of this blood that we see in this video is real blood or fake blood?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not call into question in our analyses what the investigators call a red fluid that looks like blood. We did not deal with that issue at all, whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. In your past Karadzic testimony you said: "Of course, everything, all the blood that you see in the video-clip, in my view, is real blood." And that was at transcript page 38543 of your previous Karadzic testimony. Do you stand by that testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I said a moment ago that we did not call it into question at all, whether it is real blood or not. We did not deal with that matter at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraphs 59 and 60, you discuss the depth of the crater. You raise issue with the overall depth of the crater being 9 centimetres, equalling 90 millimetres. This is on the basis of Mirza Sabljica's testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not 900 millimetres, it's 90 millimetres. 900 millimetres is almost a metre, and there should not be any confusion. We did not claim that. It was all stated based on Sabljica's report and their records. It's something that we took from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, this was translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it it was. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you realise that Mr. Sabljica's evidence is not that the overall depth of the crater was 9 centimetres, but that was a measurement from just the asphalt surface to the back end of the tail-fin while it was in the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For the Chamber's reference, in this case, this testimony can be found at transcript pages 8064 to -65, and page 8134.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You must have checked Mr. Sabljica's evidence on this and realised this when you were writing your report; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, we did, and we discussed it here, and I suppose you saw that in our submission. The fact is the depth of the crater cannot be measured from the surface of the embedded stabiliser to the surface of the ground. Such a measure did not exist. In that case, any surface into which the stabiliser did not embed itself completely could not be a crater. That's an error. I don't want to go into it now, but obviously what they needed to do was to confirm Zecevic's claim on television that the crater was more than 220 millimetres deep. And then if Sabljica is correct, we come to 250 or 300. The crater is where the stabiliser is embedded in the ground, not what is above.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So -- ma'am --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- if the stabiliser did not embed itself at all, then this would be incorrect. We know that from all that we have discussed before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the witness refers to what Mr. Zecevic told on television. Is that in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As a follow-up question --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I didn't mean to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's -- I just wanted to know because we have no possibility at this moment to verify what the witness said. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, please stay focused on my questions. You indicated that you reviewed Mr. Sabljica's evidence. Now, you're aware that actually Mr. Sabljica went to the market-place on the 5th of February and Mr. Zecevic didn't go there until the 6th; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Sabljica was there on the 5th and Zecevic was there on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You discussed the stalls in the market-place throughout your analysis of Markale I. This is throughout different times in paragraphs 3 through 78 of the report. After reading through everything, I came to your statement in paragraph 78 where you say: "As is known, the market has been renovated. The stalls have been replaced by new ones, and it is no longer possible to measure the stalls." Do you stand by that statement in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your analysis of the stalls was based on images taken from -- on different dates from different perspectives; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the sketch provided by Mr. Zecevic with the measurements he took. We used all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You appear to come up with some measurements for the stalls and other items in your report from the images. These are ones that you then appear to annotate on photos from different distances, and these photos are from different distances and different perspectives from what appears to be above, below, or to the side of the object that you are measuring. These limitations impact the precision of the measurements; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, that's not true. The basic measures were taken from a position which is practically direct to the object of filming. The supports are lateral. All the measures were taken in one or two ways to determine the margin of error, to arrive finally at an accurate, highly accurate, size of the stall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You realise that the impact -- or the explosion occurred in the rear north-east corner of the outdoor market; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It did not happen in the centre of the market?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 75, you state: "The logical question that arises is why, in seven investigations, then you mention four items related to the investigations," then you continue, "no one checked whether it was possible for the mortar shell to land on the ground without first hitting the stall roof." You state this after reviewing all the UN materials and the BiH investigative reports related to Markale I; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You then realise, for example, that the UN investigative report, Exhibit P538, which you cite throughout your -- your own report, specifically details its analysis of the height of the bursts in relation to the stalls; right? This can be found on page 10 of the English ; page 13 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They provide a report as to where the impact was compared to the stall which was there, and this is just a co-ordinate. They did not determine the minimal angle of descent compared to the height of the roof of the stall. Those are different measurements. The measurements that were given were relative to the table of the stall, not the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 78, you indicate that you believe that the market incident was "well planned, organised and implemented act of sabotage." This is your theory; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my conclusion based on all the analysis we carried out, the material evidence on the market and the surrounding buildings, after analysing the direction of fire, the traces, and analysing the possibility for the projectile to land without first hitting a roof. That was analysed in great detail with very wide margins of possibilities, and there is simply no other conclusion available.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see you're giving your standard answer when incidents come up, but I just want to go quickly through --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. We've heard this before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll proceed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's commenting on the evidence of the witness which I should refrain from doing. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to go, then, through some of the people who were or were not a part of this conspiracy. You do not think that the BiH MUP investigators like Mirza Sabljica were part of the act of sabotage or conspiracy; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't. And I don't go into thinking or analysing who could possibly be part of that conspiracy. What I dealt with was analysis of the traces and the possibility for these traces to be consistent, to conform to a certain type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like -- so we have a clear record, I'd like to go through some other individuals. None of the UN personnel or investigators were part of the conspiracy; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from asking me such questions because I do not have an answer to them. That would be speculation. It would not be serious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to tell Mr. Weber what questions to be asked. If you say it's -- it would be speculation, then just answer the question, say: I can't answer the question because it would come down to speculation. Rather than to tell Mr. Weber what questions he should put to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you answer my question? You have reviewed the UN materials related to this. None of the --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You reviewed the UN materials related to this. So, in your view, were any of the UN personnel or investigators a part of this conspiracy?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: She hasn't answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She said that she would have to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ... let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the question was asked but not answered. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, please. Page 28, line 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness commented on that it would come down to speculation, so now then I invited her to say so if that would be the answer to a question. And the question was put again to her, and if she thinks it would be speculation, then we now expect perhaps that answer. But it is -- the question was not answered directly, and, therefore, Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I was waiting a little to -- to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, it's fine --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, I will answer. I have no reason to believe any such thing, and anything I would now say, pointing a finger at anyone who was part of that investigation, would be speculation. The only thing I can say is that I found it very strange that some of the observations of the UN personnel did not find their way into the final report. For instance, the finding of Captain Verdy was not part of the final analysis, and there is no specific explanation for that. It's something we noticed, but, again, I'm not pointing a finger at anyone because that would make no sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's your evidence that the UN investigators did not consider the initial opinions by Captain Verdy as a part of their analysis? Are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say that Captain Verdy was the only one who determined the angle of descent --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am -- ma'am, that's not --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which was large and which would be consistent with --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please answer my question. Is it your evidence that the UN investigators did not consider the initial opinions by Captain Verdy as part of their analysis?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not take it into account and they did not explain why they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have no reason to believe that any of the civilians in the market-place were part of some conspiracy; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to even think about it because I have no parameters for forming an opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You comment a lot on the TV crew that was in the area. Do you believe that they were part of some conspiracy?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not claiming for a moment that anyone was part of a conspiracy, nor do we suspect anyone. We just noted that the TV crew arrived extremely quickly, because they were practically around the corner when the incident happened. And many witnesses say that. That is absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, witness, if you say that you do not claim that anyone was part of a conspiracy, then there would be no conspiracy, isn't it? Because if there are no persons involved in a conspiracy ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not true. I am not claiming that no one was part of any conspiracy. That's not what I said. I just answered the question, saying that I have no reason to suspect anyone in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, "in particular" is then -- gives the clue which I was looking for. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For Markale I, your position in the Karadzic case was that the two stationary -- was that there were two stationary mortars which were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position in the Karadzic case was that at the site that had been investigated, there had certainly been a 120-millimetre shell that was detonated under stationary conditions in a regular way, and then at the other place it could have been a shell, it could have been something else. We did not investigate that. Only Mr. Berko Zecevic marked that, and we marked the traces last week here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the Karadzic case, at transcript page 38538 to -39, Judge Kwon asked to you confirm an answer. He said: "Yes. The witness answered to a different -- when asked whether it's your position that the two mortar bombs were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device, your answer was yes; correct?" You stated: "Correct." Do you stand by that evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I just said now that there is this possibility, that some other shell had been detonated or some other device. Because we were not in a position to record these traces. No one did that during the investigations. It could have been a mortar shell placed under static conditions, like the first one that had been analysed. It also could have been another device. We do not have technical parameters. Nothing was recorded. It's only the location of the explosion that we saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, what was read to you was your answer to a question, whether it was your position that the two mortar bombs were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device, and it was read to you that your answer was: "Correct." You were then asked whether you stand by that evidence, and you said: "Yes, correct. I just said now that there is this possibility ..." Now, there's a difference between saying that it's my position that the two mortar bombs were detonated either using a timer or a remote control device or to say that that is a possibility. Do I understand that you do not claim that this is what happened but that you consider it a possibility that this may have happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I allow for the possibility that there might have been another explosive device at the other location because, I repeat, we were not in a position to analyse the traces on asphalt because they were not recorded at all. I stand by everything I said, but I do open the possibility that at the second location there may have been another explosive device and that both of them were statically activated. There is no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say you "open the possibility" and then you later say "there's no doubt about that." Is there no doubt about that possibility or is there no doubt about that having happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no doubt that there was static explosion at the place that was investigated and the place that was not investigated. There is no doubt about that. As for the place where there was no investigation, there could have been a static explosion of one shell and it also could have been another explosive device. We don't have information about that. But there are traces that we saw and we are therefore assured that there was an explosion there as well, as marked by Mr. Zecevic at the location of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I put it to you that you're shifting somewhat your theory that you presented previously in the Karadzic case, in that previously there was two mortars that caused -- that -- and you acknowledge two -- two explosions that caused a single crater, and here it appears that you're saying that there's one mortar that exploded and possibly some other type of device and you're describing two locations.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing I changed. There was one location that was investigated, and it is clear that there was an explosion there of 120-millimetre shell. There was also another explosion that was recorded. Mr. Zecevic wrote that, signed that. There is impact of shrapnel there. And, again, most probably, it was the explosion, the static explosion of a 120-millimetre shell. However, we did not have the opportunity to investigate that, so I allow for the possibility that it could have been another explosive device, and that's the only difference --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was there since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying is the difference. You're adding that in, that last part in your testimony here now in this case.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think that it's more precise if I say it this way. More precise. Quite simply, there is no photo documentation that indicates traces on the surface so that we could discuss whether it is an artillery projectile, whether it's an explosive device, whether it's a 120-millimetre shell. I assume that it is most probable that there were two shells of 120-millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I've already read in your previous confirmation to Judge Kwon about it being two mortars. You're changing your testimony now, too, to say it was from two mortars to one mortar and possibly something else; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right because that's most probable.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that Ms. Subotic explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that Ms. Subotic explained everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- put to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- say again the same thing if Mr. Weber wants, but everything is in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber can put the question as he did, and the witness may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I believe the witness has answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Were both -- this mortar and now this some other device that you're describing, were they both set up on stands?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 120-millimetre mortar shell that was analysed both by UNPROFOR and the CSB investigators were certainly placed under an angle of about 60 or 70 degrees, and it was activated statically. Because that can be concluded very simply on the basis of traces --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So you're --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on the asphalt --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So you're saying one was set up on a stand, I guess, there. What about the other one or whatever it is that you're now describing in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it must have been placed somewhere on something, but there are no traces, and we cannot say whether it is under an angle, whether it's not under an angle, whether on a stall, beneath a stall. Actually, the place of impact can be seen, it was marked clearly, but we cannot say how it was placed because we did not see the traces very clearly and very well. Quite simply it was not investigated as such. It appeared practically after the cross-examination of Mr. Zecevic and after we had insight into the video footage, where we saw traces that absolutely cannot be due to the projectile that had been investigated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I see you're now claiming that there's some other thing. Okay. Would the mortar have exploded first or this some other device that was somewhere in the market exploded beforehand?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't know that. There are witnesses who heard two explosions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's an answer to the question. You, of course, do not know that. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For your theory to be correct, some highly organised sabotage team would have had to carry out measurements in advance of placing the mortar that you've described on some type of stand, with those measurements being very carefully calculated to be consistent with the mortar having come from Bosnian Serb-held territory; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and we wrote that. And you skipped a stage during this description of yours. And that is to say that beforehand the stabiliser was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, we'll go through some different stages here. You agree that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness finish her sentence --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said: "And that is to say that beforehand the stabiliser was ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The stabiliser was dug into the surface and then above it there was this montage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So now the mortar did not have a stabiliser on it. It was pre- -- somehow under the ground somehow before the explosion. Is that what you're saying? I just want to understand.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're trying to understand very well. That is what I'm trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If there was a secondary device which was attached to the mortar, you would expect to find physical evidence of that secondary device at the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, you are right, but I believe that there are ways used by saboteurs to leave minimal traces, if any at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There was no evidence in what you inspected to suggest that the physical remains of a timer or secondary remote control device was found at the scene; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After a mortar and some other explosive device detonated in the market-place, that must have killed a lot of people; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And ever since you put your question, I have been thinking, these two explosions probably took place at the same time or almost at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under your theory of what happened, there must have been bodies in the market-place of those who were killed in the detonations and then very quickly more bodies were brought into the market-place and scattered or placed around the bodies of those who had just been killed. Are you saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the film that was shot during the evacuation, there is every indication that that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. It follows, then, that there must have been a pile of bodies dressed in civilian clothing stored very close to the market-place prior to the incident, and they were dragged out after the detonation; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably that's what happened. And you've already seen that there were many illogical things that happened during this evacuation and that would indicate that that kind of thing did happen, starting with the area towards Marsala Tita Street being closed, then there was no traffic in Marsala Tita, it went in the opposite direction. And then an ambulance arrived with one corpse already in it and that was recorded and so on and so forth. And then corpses were moved under which there were no traces of blood. You saw all of that. In this analysis these are some of the things that we observed and that we certainly thought we should draw attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The bodies must have been taken from wherever they were stored prior to the detonation, placed in the market by what you've described as a well-organised sabotage team, and then those same bodies were brought to the Kosevo hospital all within 20 minutes; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was exactly all. We were not doing any counting. And on of the basis of this film, we were not in a position to count whether all the persons who were on the truck were already dead and then transported to the Kosevo hospital. These are questions that I'm not a position to answer, that I cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In my question I don't believe I said "all." In your previous Karadzic testimony, at transcript page 38543 to -44, you were asked: "Q. It follows, does it not, that the bodies must have been taken from wherever they were stored prior to the detonation, placed in the market-place by what you've described as a well-organised sabotage team, and those -- then those same bodies were brought to the Kosevo hospital within those 20 minutes?" Your answer was: "Correct." That's what you stated during the Karadzic case; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it is correct. Yes, of course, they were taken away. Of course, I didn't do any counting. I was not in a position to do any kind of counting. After all, you saw that these numbers do not tally even in the records --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, you're --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- let alone that I do the counting as I watch this film.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Doesn't it follow from your theory that the sabotage crew had access to a good number of human beings who were dead and who were in civilian clothing and who happened to bear signs of injuries consistent with a detonation from a mortar projectile?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, on the ground when there's a war going on, there are casualties, fatalities on a daily basis. Quite a few people get killed. Then in the mortuary we also had cases when people died of other -- I mean, there were at least three, as far as I can remember, died from wounds inflicted by fire-arms. So we were not in a position to see all the injuries that you are speaking about. But it is certain that there was a large number of dead people and wounded people during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Under your theory, there were at least four visits by this highly professional sabotage team to the crowded market where the mortar exploded. The first visit was when they embedded the stabiliser. The second visit was after the stabiliser was removed in order to create an angle of descent of 60 degrees in the hole. The third visit was after Verdy was at the scene but before Russell got there, an hour after Verdy had left to adjust the angle supposedly from 60 to 70 degrees. And the fourth visit was after Russell had left to adjust the angle back from 70 degrees to 60 degrees. Have I missed any of the visits of the sabotage team from your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is one possibility. The other possibility is a lot more pragmatic, and that is that the stabiliser was dug in. And there is footage to that effect after the explosion, what the place looked like, where it was stuck. Then the shell had been placed under an angle for remote activation. All of that can be done on one occasion. All the rest could have been left during the events that evolved. As we know, everybody was digging and trying to get their own, so there's no reason. They could have left it all very nicely to develop as it was already developing. The only thing that was important was that this stabiliser was deeply dug in all along its length so that it would be sure that the possibility would be removed of firing coming from BH-held territory. All the rest could have happened without any major influence on the course of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I put it to you that an infinitely more likely scenario and explanation for what happened on the 5th of February, 1994, was that mortar projectile was, in fact, fired from Bosnian Serb positions and hit the market-place. Did you consider that possibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, you did see that we took into account that possibility. That possibility is totally excluded, number one, by the direction of the trajectory that was established on the ground. Number two, for this direction, the height and the form of the stall make it absolutely impossible for the projectile to fall and be activated in the place where it fell and where it was activated without affecting the stall. And we show that very clearly, and we indicated all the possibilities that were indispensable for ascertaining this and checking this. And thirdly, there are traces that show that the shell was activated underneath the stall. And two UNPROFOR investigators registered that. So, of course, we took all of that into account and, of course, that that was impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to start another little area. I don't know if -- I see it's a couple of minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a couple of minutes before the break. Let's take the break now. Ms. Subotic, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, is it your evidence that the sabotage team who buried the stabiliser had access to jackhammer or some kind of heavy instrument to drill through the hard asphalt surface of the Markale market in order to bury the stabiliser at a precise depth that would make it appear to be -- to have been fired from distance?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not making any claims as to what instrument it was done with, but it was certainly dug into the ground for the explosive device to be placed there. I cannot talk about which tool was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the Karadzic case, it appears that you left open the possibility of whether or not the stabiliser was buried before or after and it -- also according to page 33 -- I'm sorry, 38558 to -59, it was your position that someone used a hand tool, like a spade, to dig through the asphalt and plant the stabiliser. You've never tried to dig through an asphalt surface with a spade; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never tried to dig anything with a spade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And just so we have it in the record, the question that was posed to was: "Ms. Subotic, have you ever tried to dig through a tarmac surface with a spade? " Your answer was: "No, of course, not. However, I had my heel, a complete heel, get into the asphalt. Honestly, I don't want to interfere with other people's areas of expertise. I'm sure that he needed a tool of some sort, but whether that should have been a jackhammer, I'm really convinced that it didn't." That was your previous testimony; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard in my headset as the interpretation, with all due respect to everyone, I certainly never uttered because I never mentioned a whole heel in my whole testimony. It's quite possible that any kind of tool was used, any kind of instruments. I really cannot go into that because I don't know. I was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, would you please again read to the witness what is recorded as her testimony slowly so that we avoid any misinterpretations. Mr. Lukic, I'm asking your specific attention on whether there will be any problems as far as translation is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was corrected in B/C/S already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was corrected already in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's why Ms. Subotic laughed and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, of course, we do not know what was corrected. Could you perhaps, Mr. Weber, again read it, and now apparently we do not expect any further translation issues, and then put the question again to the witness so that she can answer it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "Q. Ms. Subotic, have you ever tried to dig through a tarmac surface with a spade? "A. No, of course, not. However, I had my heel, a complete heel, get into the asphalt. Honestly, I don't want to interfere with other people's areas of expertise. I'm sure that he needed a tool of some sort, but whether that should have been a jackhammer, I'm really convinced that it didn't." That was your previous testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are aware that another ballistics expert named Derek Allsop testified for the Defence of Mr. Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In terms of chronology, Dr. Allsop testified before you in the Karadzic case. Did you review or consider either his expert testimony or his reports when completing your Markale report in either the last case or this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we did see him and we did not use his evidence. We saw him at the time we worked on the Karadzic case. We did not use his reports then or now. I'm not sure about then, but certainly not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Dr. Allsop was initially listed as a Defence expert in the Mladic case. Did you have any conversations with him about your Markale report, your current Markale report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33116 for the witness, e-court page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your testimony in the Karadzic case, which is now before you, Mr. Karadzic asked you about Dr. Allsop's static explosion conclusions. At line 8, you were asked: "Q. Defence witness Derek Allsop said that he did not support the thesis which indicated that this was a static explosion because the stabiliser could not have become embedded in the ground in that way. What is your opinion of it?" You answered: "I viewed this testimony and the gentleman is right because he was looking at a specific case. Had the static explosion taken place there and the stabiliser been positioned on the shell, then it would not have been possible because the shell did not fly in and there would not have been that speed that we referred to. It would not have been possible for the stabiliser to become embedded in the ground. I agree so far. But this implies the fact that a shell complete with a stabiliser is statically activated. That's the only scenario that is being considered here." Do you stand by your past testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That specific case that Dr. Allsop was looking at was the Markale I events; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33120 for the witness, page 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to go through some portions of Dr. Allsop's testimony in the Karadzic case. Before you is the transcript of his testimony where there was a discussion of the different theories concerning Markale I. Starting at the top of the page, Dr. Allsop was asked: "The first is a theory concerning the Markale I incident. Now, the Judges have heard a witness refer to a theory that the incident was caused by a roof-top delivery of a 120-millimetre projectile from a building of five or more storeys into the market-place down below. Do you accept that theory?" Dr. Allsop stated: "No." "Q. Could you explain why you do not? "A. There are a number of reasons. The first reason is that all of these projectiles, then they have a fuse for a very good reason. One is, of course, to initiate the explosive when it impacts the target, but an important feature is for it to be safe in storage and so that the -- when the projectile is actually -- before it's fired, if you dropped it, it would not initiate it because the fuse prevents it from doing so. And so that when the projectile is fired, it arms the fuse and it does this by the setback forces. The acceleration is thousands of G, you know, so that the actual setback forces on the fuse is extremely high. And so it's those setback fuses that actually arm the fuse and have to somehow -- if you had a conventional -- if you just had a 120-millimetre mortar bomb, then you would have to find some way -- if you were going to drop it from a building, you would have to have some way of arming the fuse. And the -- just -- I think you might be able to do it if you hit the back of it with a sledge hammer, but if you did that, that might mark the back of the fins and you would see that on the subsequent fin. So that's one of the reasons." I'll pause here. You agree with Dr. Allsop's reasons stated so far, correct, that a roof-top delivery was not possible for these reasons?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically his views are correct. However, he did not take into account the possibility that the fuse may have been removed before the shell being dropped, and it's quite possible to change this chain of occurrences. That was often done on the front line. And I even worked on cases where the enemy forces left hand-grenades armed for use without any fuse. If we take that possibility into account, then this version you just describe does not quite hold up to scrutiny. But if you discount that, then the rest is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
