utterances.text: A fuse is what activates the mortar upon impact; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By momentum or upon impact, depending on the way it set up. But that's not the point of this witness was talking about. The point is that there is some security factor that could be overcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue on. Dr. Allsop goes on to provide another reason. He states at line 25, continuing on to the next page: "The other" -- and this is Dr. Allsop: "The other reason is no matter how you threw it, if you threw it, dropped it, or whatever, it would almost certainly drop vertically, and so that means that the pattern on the ground of the fragments would, in fact, be almost perfectly symmetrical. Although it's actually difficult to see the fragmentation pattern of the 120-millimetre mortar on the ground, the one that was actually fired, it does actually show that, in fact, it was -- it did impact at an angle. So those are my main reasons for discounting the theory." Do you accept that Dr. Allsop also considered in -- a factor for why it was not thrown from the roof the actual pattern on the ground? Do you agree that that's a relevant factor?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see that he believed that a shell, if it is somehow manually dropped, probably falls at an angle of 90 degrees and leaves that kind of pattern. That's rather logical. Although he did not explain how come that it can be dropped and activated that way, whereas the moment before he was saying it's impossible. I think the statement you read out a moment ago from the same witness contradicts this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's read on. Dr. Allsop was also asked the following starting at line 12: "Q. Now, in the scenario that's been raised before the Court, the projectile was thrown from the top of a building of about 15 and a half metres in height so that it landed on the ground a minimum distance of 11.1 metres away from the base of that building I've just described. Do you accept that as a likely trajectory, if I may say so, or a likely scenario for the Markale I incident?" Dr. Allsop's answer: "No, no. I -- as I explained at our meeting, then I don't think it would be physically possible to throw a 12 and a half kilogram projectile 11 metres." Do you agree with him on this one?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the gentleman probably meant that one person could not do that. I cannot estimate, really. I don't know what he meant, that one person cannot do it, that it cannot be dropped using some kind of support or tool. I cannot agree or disagree with this because I don't know what he meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Continuing on, Dr. Allsop was asked: "Q. It's further been suggested that someone ran out after the explosion in the midst of the dead and dying victims and plugged the stabiliser into the ground before the arrival of UNPROFOR officials or ... Bosnian police officials. Do you accept that this is a possible scenario?" Dr. Allsop answered: "I find that highly unlikely. I've already been talking about the fuse" furrow "and this actually entering into a pre-formed hole formed by a -- a fuse falling directly behind the fuse. The appearance in the video then -- that's exactly what I would expect, that it has all of the characteristics of a 120-millimetre mortar bomb strike." Mr. Karadzic's other expert disagreed with you; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant when he said this. In any case, we saw that that crater is not consistent with the usual situation after impact, and we saw that at the place where it was embedded there is buried material. It had to be dug out, which is impossible. When a shell flies in and the stabiliser is embedded, that doesn't happen. I don't know what he said -- meant when he said he saw what he expected to see. Maybe he saw some parts of the investigation which are typical, such as impact of shrapnel on the asphalt. But he certainly couldn't be saying that the stabiliser left a typical pattern on the surface because it is not. We have seen that many times. We've seen that image.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You disagree with Dr. Allsop that the pattern had all of the characteristics of a 120-millimetre mortar bomb strike; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would object. We should see what was shown to Mr. Allsop as Ms. Subotic mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you consider that to be relevant, then, of course, in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what was shown to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you can raise that matter in re-examination. I don't know whether anything was shown to him or not. Ms. Subotic tells us that from all of it, we can see this and that. She's not clear in what exactly she refers to. But the question, there should be no objection. The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You disagree with Dr. Allsop that the pattern had all of the characteristics of a 120-millimetre mortar bomb strike; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pattern did bear characteristics of shrapnel impact. However, the place where the stabiliser, according to the Bosnian police and UNPROFOR, got embedded during the explosion in the surface is completely atypical and is not consistent with the embedding of a stabiliser occurring after an explosion and a high-velocity flight of a projectile because it was completely buried under asphalt and I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's read on. Dr. Allsop was then asked: "Q. Now, it's further been suggested that the Markale I incident might have been a static explosion, that it occurred on the ground. The citation for that is page 12357. Dr. Allsop, do you accept the possibility that -- or do you accept that it's a likely explanation that this was a static explosion? "A. I would not accept it as a likely one. "Q. Do you accept it's even possible? " Dr. Allsop: "Possible? I -- for the same reasons, one, you've got to arm this. How did the fin actually get into the hole? The only way that ... fin could have got into the hole is because it was actually moving through the air at a higher velocity -- the projectile was moving through the air at a higher velocity and the ejection velocity of the tail-fin. So I cannot see how the ... fin would have ended up in the hole from a static explosion." Dr. Allsop disagreed with you on this; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Allsop obviously considered the only possibility that is normal in dynamics for flight. I cannot agree with him completely because he did not even consider the possibility that we described. It's true that it cannot get embedded without --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat this answer. The interpreter was unable to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please repeat your answer because the interpreters had difficulties in following you. I think you started by saying that: "Dr. Allsop obviously considered the only possibility that is normal in dynamics for flight." Could you resume from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He considered only one possibility; namely that the fins and the stabiliser embed themselves as a consequence of the velocity of flight higher than the setback force which happens after impact of mortar projectiles on the ground when there are no alterations or sabotage actions. He did not consider the possibility that the stabiliser was separated from the shell and buried before the explosion. So he could not possibly agree with something that he didn't even consider. What I see from his text is that he considered only one possibility and that is how a stabiliser gets embedded into surface under normal circumstances. That is to say, when it lands at a higher velocity, then the velocity of setback, which did not happen -- which does not happen with a shell that is buried prior to the incident into the ground. So there was no stabiliser at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may I take it that at the end of your answer you were referring to that it doesn't happen with a tail-fin that is buried prior to the incident into the ground. Is that what you wanted to say? Tail-fin or stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was translated to us as the shell being buried, but I now fully understand your answer. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Continuing on. Another scenario Dr. Allsop was asked to consider was: "Q. Right. And I'll raise one final scenario for your consideration, and that is the possibility of a 120-millimetre mortar projectile being buried under the surface of the asphalt. Do you accept that is in any way a likely scenario? Dr. Allsop: "That's not possible. You would not have had that characteristic. The asphalt's hardly been disturbed. You would expect quite a massive -- quite a massive crater formed by such an explosion." Dr. Allsop also disagreed with you about the burying of the stabiliser; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but Dr. - I cannot see the name - Allsop was asked whether it was possible that a mine should have been buried. We are not talking about a whole mine or a whole shell. We are now talking only about the stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right. Throughout your testimony, you have criticised many Prosecution experts. The fact is that a Defence ballistics expert, who was in your same field, in your last case also disagree with you -- disagreed with you. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't accept it. He did not discuss my solution but the possibilities that are correct. Except they don't relate to this problem. There are technical reasons for all the things that he did not accept, and they are not related to our claim or our analysis. There is no contradiction. Everything he said he doesn't accept is technically correct, but it does not relate to the specific situation that we wrote about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, may I revisit your last question. And Mr. Lukic did not object, but you misrepresented what Dr. Allsop said and asked the witness then whether she did disagree with that because you really presented it in an unfair way to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was not my intent, and if I misspoke, I sincerely apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, happily enough, the witness herself was able to correct you, and that's of course appreciated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's turn to Markale II on 28 August 1995. In paragraph 105, page 117 in the English and page 175 of the B/C/S, you stated: "We come to the conclusion that the shell could not have landed there, but it was, rather, activated statically or reached the pavement in front of the market hall in some other way." First, when you say "the shell," your conclusion is that one mortar shell exploded in front of the market on the 28th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since this happened out in the open, we did not have the possibility of checking whether it was one or two. As you know, there were several stabilisers which indicates that -- well, we don't have a position on this. But it indicates that something is not right during the investigation. However, since it was out in the open, we could not look at other objects as we could in Markale I, if you remember, so we could not see whether there was impact of shrapnel from a mine or shell that was not looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there one or two explosions on the 28th of August, 1995, in front of the market?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can believe that there is one and we can consider that there was one as that is what we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You leave open many possibilities, it appears, when you say alternatively that the shell could have reached the pavement "in some other way." You do this because there are no physical traces or remnants of a static activation; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. No such thing was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "in some other way"? It's not clear in your report what you're -- what theory you're getting at here.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some way, obviously, it fell there at minimal speed, as indicated by all the traces, so -- well, there's this idea that it was thrown from a roof or thrown through a window and then this idea that it was statically activated. So all options are on the table and equally plausible or probable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We looked at Dr. Allsop's testimony about why he thought the Markale I incident -- that it was not likely that it was thrown from a roof. I put it to you that those same reasons are valid concerning Markale II and whether or not it was thrown from the roof of the building above where the crater is found. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said a moment ago that I'm not sure what the doctor had in mind. He probably thought it was impossible for one man to throw 12 kilograms in such a way. I don't know how or with what kind of aid that could have happened. And once this chain was taken off the fuse, that is what protects it from explosion, if the members of the crew drop it. So I don't know what kind of aid somebody could have used for doing this. But if you look at our analysis, which is exhaustive, detailed, and well-founded, you will see that there is no possibility of -- there is no technical possibility of it arriving there either from positions of the Army of Republika Srpska or from positions that are nearby of the ABiH. Because we assume that the firing would have to have been heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- witness, could you explain exactly what you meant by "and once this chain was taken off the fuse"? Could you tell us what chain you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Allsop spoke about this safety chain and the construction of the fuse that is used for purposes of prevention. If members of the crew drop it, then in this way, it is not activated. There has to be an initial force and then the fuse can activate the mine. Once that happens, then this safety chain is removed and then the mine can be activated irrespective of the speed. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. No, perhaps just one other question. Can you take that off the fuse or do you take off the whole fuse? The chain is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a mechanism that is within the fuse and it prevents the fuse from starting the explosion until the projectile gets a certain speed during its trajectory, and that makes it impossible for it to explode if it falls by accident, if it is dropped. So you take off the fuse, take that part off, return the fuse, and it is only then that it can be activated as soon as it touches the surface at any speed. There is no need for the kind of speed that Dr. Allsop refers to in his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so it is a part of the fuse which you can remove easily? Could you explain as how you do that? Do you need a screwdriver for that? I mean, how is that embedded in the fuse, that safety chain or whatever you call it? Have you ever done that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you nevertheless explain then how to exactly do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one has to look at the construction of the fuse and see which part -- which part pertains to that stage and then that is opened and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you have to look at how it's -- what the construction is. But could you tell us, is it welded in? What -- what does it take to get that out; and how does that affect the functioning of the fuse if it's taken out? Could you give the details of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the fuse is removed from the mine and then it is opened and then that part is removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- let me stop you there. How do you open the fuse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The casing is taken off and then you get to the mechanism. The mechanism that is inside, you dismantle it the way you dismantle any device, using a screwdriver and the tools that people had and made do with during the war. People did it very skillfully. I remember doing an expert report on a particular case like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- do you have documentation which explains how to take that safety part out of the fuse? It must have been described somewhere, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first of all, the work of the mechanism of the fuse is described in its technical documentation in the PKP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether it's described how to take out that safety mechanism from a fuse, how you do that, where do have you to put the screwdriver. Is that described anywhere? I take it, it must be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably in handbooks and books of the service for counter-sabotage protection. They deal with that. Sabotage and counter-sabotage. And they have all of these details that pertain to weaponry and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. You say "probably" there, and then you say they have all the details. You're the expert. Could you tell us not where it probably is but where we can find it or how you can give it to us so that we can follow in detail what you describe as a possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some part of the construction of the fuse is contained in firing tables, but that certainly does not include such instructions, because firing tables are not intended for this kind of use. What I can recommend are, indeed, books for counter-sabotage protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question to you is: You are stating that this is a possibility. Where did you find that possibility described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't need to find the description of that possibility. I know how this construction works. I could disarm any fuse if necessary. If you are working on the construction of that and also on its verification, it's quite simple to read the drawing, how this fuse works and how it can be disarmed on a certain basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, let -- let me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because this is an action that is not a customary one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that you couldn't tell us exactly where it is described how to take out this safety feature of the fuse and -- how to take it out? You don't know where it is described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I assume that it's in these books that I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber, of course, would be interested to see whether there's any documentation on -- on how to do that. I don't know whether there's any of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The fuse would not work without the safety. The safety is what controls it arming and not arming; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. That is not correct. It does control it, but once it is bridged, it no longer controls it. You certainly looked at my expert report, and you see that I have done this kind of expertise in relation to the war and also in the case of hand-grenades as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. You just used the word "bridged." Are you saying that there then would have to be a work-around in the fuse once the safety was removed?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, then it functions directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, if the shell was placed in the middle of a busy road and statically activated, did someone from some sabotage group run out in the middle of the street while the cars were going by to do this?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer to that. I was not there and, therefore, I cannot give you an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll keep going, see if I can get through the next thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your theories appear to be based upon criticisms of the determined minimal angle of descent from the nearby building and separately the calculated angle of descent determined from the crater itself. I want to first start with the minimal angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D05496. And if we could please go to page 173 of the B/C/S version only. I'd like to look at the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 104, you discuss figure 117 which is now before us. In the paragraph you state: "On the basis of figure 117, it is estimated that the width of the frieze is about 12 centimetres." First are you referring to the frieze at the top of the building on the roof or the frieze between the second and third floors of the building?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The frieze that is at the top of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the same paragraph, you appear to go -- gone to recalculate the minimal angle of descent by subtracting these 12 centimetres related to the width of the frieze and another 6 centimetres for the mortar from the measurements that you come up with which are, as you acknowledged before that, lower than those taken by the BH MUP and UN investigators. You are assuming that the investigators did not take into consideration the shape of the mortar or the building when making their calculations; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not assuming anything. We saw how they conducted their measuring in this film that was shot, I mean, during this investigation, when speaking of the UN. On the sketch of the scene dimensions are provided, so there's no need to make any kind of assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P498, page 24 of the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the calculation of the minimum angle of descent from the MUP file. The shape of the building and, in particular, the friezes were taken into consideration by the investigators. We can all see this in the image; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please either adjust the microphone or to speak into it when answering the question. And could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that what can be see here is that the measurements were taken from the frieze. And what can also be seen is that what was not taken into account -- I mean, there's no indication that the diameter of the shell was not taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we're at the time for a break. If we could take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take the break now. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have to postpone the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, we can -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours inquired about possible information about the fuse, and I would just note for the record that admitted as Exhibit P4211, which is 120-millimetre mortar manual, and with respect to the relevant fuse type, based on the information in Exhibit P498 we would note that that is an M62 fuse. And we would just note for the record, English e-court pages 82 to 84 of P4211, and we would draw significant attention to paragraph 383. And also in the B/C/S version, figure 84 on page 115 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that. Do we find -- apart from a description of the fuse, do we also find there, and I apologise for not having all of the evidence, especially documentary evidence, on the top of my head, but will we find what I specifically asked for, how to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's not step by step in that way but it explains the construction of the fuse and the functioning of the fuse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D5496, page 176 of the B/C/S version only. I'd like to look at the figure on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, I'm going to turn to the angle of descent based on the crater. In your report it appears that you've recalculated the centre of the explosive mass for the mortar which is illustrated before us from what the investigators determined, which was just a shade under 188 millimetres, to what you feel it is, which is 240 millimetres. I put it to you that you've simply created an imaginary cone which, according to you, is the shape of the explosive charge; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. We have this cone that follows the cone-like explosive and we used another method to check the centre of the mass provided by the Bosnian investigators, whether it is closer or the one that we gave. And we gave ours on the basis of documentation about this, that is 240, that is the centre according to us. And this is just an illustration without any kind of major calculations that would just encumber this paper. It just confirms that the explosive charge is there. This is just one analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First, as we can see from the shape of the mortar itself, it is not shaped in a cone but it is more of a -- what I would describe as a pointed tear drop. Based on the actual shape of a mortar, the investigators correctly placed the centre of the explosive mass where it belongs and not you; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. And I will very gladly, if the Court asks me to do that, I will send an excerpt from documents where, I mean, this information is contained after all. My colleague Vukasinovic who was the protagonist of the research precisely for this shell used the same values in his analysis and we worked together. And firing tables are worked out without this kind of information. Please do trust me, that that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, you're going to my next question here. You got the 240-millimetre measurement from Miroljub Vukasinovic, his un-peer-tested symposium paper; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my colleague Dr. Miroljub Vukasinovic we took this over, and I did not quite understand what you were getting, because I don't really know what this pertains to. And you said "unpeered." I don't know what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. The 250 -- the 240-millimetre measurement that you used came from Miroljub Vukasinovic's symposium paper on Markale II; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he presented at some symposium. And he took it from the technical documentation from the military technical institute for that shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm asking you that's where you got it from?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 106 of your report, do I understand correctly that you yourself acknowledge that his findings were wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the calculations, he took some figures that were wrong, but that is -- well, that did not significantly affect his findings. He took figures related to the crater erroneously and instead of the centre of the mass of the explosive, he took the centre of the mass of the shell when carrying out this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's move on. You have never operated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to come back to one of the previous questions; that is, whether the shape of the building was considered and whether the diameter of the mortar shell was considered. I think you said: Well, whatever they did with the building, at least they ignored the -- the diameter of the shell. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did understand me well. There is this discrepancy in measurements and we checked that. You probably saw that -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, these 6 centimetres, what effect would that have had on the angle of descent or the angle of impact? I think it's also Pythagoras, more or less. We apparently are stuck with him. Could you calculate for us what the difference in outcome would be if you would include those 6 centimetres, how much would that affect the minimum angle of descent? Are you in a position to do that? Not now immediately but perhaps during one of the breaks or perhaps if we do not finish today this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, maybe it would be good give her instruction if it's based on 6 centimetres down from what the investigators determined, or 6 centimetres what she feels, or both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps for both. But I would like to have an impression as to how this -- what you present as negligence, how this affects the outcome. If would you do that perhaps both for your own calculations and for the findings in the report which were contemporaneously [indiscernible] -- I would highly appreciate if you would do that. And could you limit yourself to my question rather than to write a whole new paper on the matter. I'm just merely interested in if you included in your calculations what would the outcome be in degrees as far as the minimum angle of descent is concerned, nothing else. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have never operated a Cymbeline radar system; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You do not know that these Cymbeline radar systems can be pointed in different directions known as arcs; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I read reports compiled by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The extent of your knowledge about Cymbeline radar systems relates to the reports for the Markale II events; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And statements that UNPROFOR provided in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter -- it's actually the same one that's up on the screen. 1D5496, page 195 of the B/C/S only. I'm seeking to go to figure 139.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before us is figure 139 of your Markale report. You have a dashed horizontal line in this figure which appears to represent the floor where the radar would supposedly detect the incoming projectile at 548 metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your source for the 548 metres. Where did you get this figure from?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's from the UNPROFOR report that says that this radar would register every shell fired from 900 millimetres [as interpreted] and that is 550 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it your claim that the UNPROFOR report -- or UNPROFOR -- the ones that you reviewed, uses the figure 548 metres?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance is used fired from 900 metres and that distance is from the firing tables, 548 metres. What is written there is that any shell fired from a distance of 900 metres and more than that, it would have been registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking for a real simple answer. The 548 metres is not -- not contained in the UNPROFOR report. That's some other deduction that you're making?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That follows from the 900 metres firing distance at which the radar is set, that the radar can observe, and that's how the tables were made. It's not an exact value. It's according to the tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's see if we can get this a little different way. Now, it appears that you placed a representation of the crater, of the centre point, in the maximum diameter of the radar's beam. The centre point, if I'm understanding that, to be at least -- to be over 1.000 metres above the market. What is your source for where you place the centre point of the radar beam?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the position of the radar, as far as I understood the report. It was described based on the fact that this radar beam could catch all the shells from charge 1 to charge 6 as you see it sketched here in this part where all these trajectories meet. Because the altitudes are so high, the radar couldn't catch them if it was set up further away. To catch all the shells, it had to be set at a distance where it is at the crossing point of all the trajectories, as you see in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The UNPROFOR documents you cite in your report, and specifically I think you have been referring to the memorandum from Colonel Powers admitted as part of P797, these materials do not contain any indication of the altitude of the centre point of the radar beam above the market on the 28th of August. I put it to you again that you have no source for the information in this graph, do you?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. The data on this graph was drawn based on the fact that in the UNPROFOR report it was written that the Cymbeline radar would register every shell fired from a distance of 900 metres. If you take into account the specifications of that shell, it looks the way we have drawn it here. It's the correct altitude and there's nothing inaccurate about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This schematic is not an accurate representation of what is depicted; correct? And I'd -- even just to help you out with your answer here, in the Karadzic case at transcript pages 38570 to -71, when commenting on this, you stated: "Secondly, you mistook a schematic representation for an accurate depiction, because in the latter case I would have given the ordinate values, and then you could have read them and interpreted the value that you say -- you stated." You then on went to say: "This diagram does not have a scale, and it is merely an illustration to help the reader understand what is being discussed, and it is meant for you to read values from an ordinate which doesn't have a scale." This is correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is that not exactly what figure 139 says? Last line: "Note that details are shown only for illustration and are not true to scale."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just confirming that this is not necessarily an accurate depiction. Because she also said that "you mistook this schematic representation for an accurate depiction ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's in the report itself, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is she acknowledging that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it that if she doesn't step back from her report and we take that as what her position is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, we also see in this chart that are you using values for M49 shell or Russian OF473. This is an old heavy mortar which has different values in the tables than the light mortars; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. But you know why? It's used because UNPROFOR used their graphic tables for firing to explain this unbelievable idea that the shell flew under the radar, and now you have a problem understanding why I'm analysing something different than what what was analysed by people initially. UNPROFOR did their own analysis and provided that table in their report on page ... I'll find it. Let me not waste your time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The footprint of a 120-millimetre mortar tube - meaning -- what I'm referring to is the amount of space that it occupies when being deployed in the field - is about 2 square metres; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You wanted to say that 2 square metres is an area where a mortar, the weapon, is set? Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When a 120-millimetre mortar is deployed in the field, it occupies a space of about 2 square metres; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to page 200 of the B/C/S of this same report, 1D5496.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is an image that you've addressed previously and made calculations about in the Karadzic case. I will, like the last time, describe it as a pie slice. It is a slice of what appears to be 5.000 metres in length and extending from 175 to 150 degrees; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this line in the shape of an arch -- of an arc? 175 to 180. But if you meant this arc underneath which is 150 ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the total area covered by what I'm describing, as it was to you the last time, as a pie slice of -- from the very top, down the side, it appears to be 5.000 metres, and then if you -- the total area within this slice which extends between 175 and 150 degrees. Do you understand what I'm referring to? Same thing that was referred to last time. You made calculations about this; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm asking you to confirm your previous calculations. The total area covered in this pie slice is 5.454.153.9 square metres of which 4.51 million square metres of surface area falls within the control of the Army of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I calculated it somewhere and you are using now my calculations, then you should give me a reference. I don't know how much it amounts to looking at this pie slice. I don't know whether what you are saying is correct or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At transcript page 38595 of the Karadzic case you stated: "The latter figure, 5454" -- I'll just start again. "... 5454153.9. This is the entire circular piece. However, from that piece, another piece should be subtracted which was under the BH control which is 872.664, so that in fact you did provide the exact figure in your first calculation," which was 4.51 million. Do you stand by these numbers?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Million what? Metres?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Million square metres.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Square metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I calculated it that way last time, then, yes, that's it's way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you have any reason to think that that's not the calculation, if you could please let us know in the morning, that would be great. You did not inspect this entire area during your two-day visit in 2010; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we inspected all parts of that area that were possible to inspect, and we provided the results. And we stated that we found only one place where it was possible to set up a mortar and it's in the direction of 186.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "186," are you saying 186 degrees?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 176. I said azimuth 176, 176.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see how far I get. I want to move on to your modified air bomb report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Unless Your Honours have any other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I want to move on to your modified air bomb report and start with a few simple questions for the remainder of today. First, an air bomb is not shaped like a round ball. It is larger towards the front and then it becomes more narrow towards the end of the bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on the shape of an air bomb, its weight is distributed more towards the front or the top of the bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of the mass, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you check the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, the transcript records you in response to my last question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been corrected, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Air bombs are designed to be dropped from the air and land at a near vertical angle; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Air bombs are unguided projectiles; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: 100-kilogram and 250-kilogram air bombs are highly destructive; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One carries 49 kilos of explosive and the other one around 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A significant portion of your modified air bomb report appears to be spent trying to create some criticism of Berko Zecevic over some sort of difference between the blast effects of fuel air bombs and TNT-filled air bombs, even at times where I could not find Mr. Zecevic making the conclusions you state. The fact is that the blast effects of fuel air bombs are not in any way different from the effects on targets of aircraft bombs filled with TNT or other solid explosives; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is absolutely incorrect. I'm very sorry that I have to answer like this, but these are two completely different effects along two completely different principles, two completely different explosives with diametrically opposite effects at the place where they are activated and where the effects of their action occur. We described that in detail. I'm very surprised that you couldn't find it because we referenced everything to Zecevic's report. And the basic difference is - I really have to say this - TNT is a highly explosive projectile, that's its purpose. And bombs with different explosives are very different, with completely different characteristics, and their purpose is, of course, different. Depending on the extra pressure in the explosion with a spreading explosion, as opposed to TNT, which is solid, every aspect of their action is different, so I don't see where you found this similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 33190, page 90 of the English and page 82 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up will be the expert report of your -- one of your co-authors, Ms. Andjelkovic Lukic. And I'm focusing on section 6.79. In the previous sections, Ms. Andjelkovic Lukic in her report is discussing the effects of fuel air bombs. And then in section 6.79, entitled "Effects on target," she states: "These are not in any way different from the effects on targets of aircraft bombs filled with TNT or other solid explosives ..." This is where I'm getting it from. Do you accept your author's -- your co-author's statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that at the analysed place what she sees is in no way different from the FAB-100 bomb filled with TNT. And that's true. She analysed a specific place and said that this impact is no different from the effects of the FAB-100 bomb filled with TNT. But it's not true that she said that it's in no way different from the effects of a dispersion bomb. Please, let's not mix apples and oranges. She analysed a specific location and said it's no different from the FAB-100 bomb filled with TNT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could the witness tell us exactly where it is clear that in paragraph 6.79 - because that's what we're looking at - where it is found that she considered here not the effects on target in general terms, but, rather, only in relation to a certain incident or certain situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's clearly written. "Effects on target: These are not in any way different from the effects on targets of aircraft bombs filled with TNT or other solid explosives and they are also not linked to the established" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please, if you read, you have the -- you -- you speed up in -- so could you please slowly re-start reading. Perhaps from -- no, if you just read from the beginning, that's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 6.79, "Effects on target": "These are not in any way different from the effects on targets of aircraft bombs filled with TNT or other solid explosives, and they are also not linked to the established documentary evidence by means of a relevant evidentiary procedure. Figure 8 (page 00378670) is a photograph of a modified FAB-100 aircraft bomb, which did not explode at the target, and the question is why this bomb was not used to identify the type of explosive used. There is no information at all in the documents under consideration as to what was done with that bomb and whether it was tested, except for the [sic] photograph of it which is shown in a couple of places in these documents (point 5.20 of this analysis)." So she analysed the effects in a certain place and said that they are no different from the effects of a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there. Where is it said or where do we find that she is not talking in general terms but that she analyses a specific situation? I don't see it in 6.79 but perhaps it's somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have the complete previous part of what our co-author wrote, but there is this sentence that clearly says: "The effects on target are no different from the effects of FAB-100 filled with TNT or any other explosive." And from that, it follows that she analysed the effects in a certain place and concluded that these were the effects of a bomb FAB-100 filled with TNT. On the basis of which one can certainly not make the conclusion that was made by the Prosecutor when he asked me that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've heard your answer. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: FAB-100s and FAB-250s -- I'll back up one. Air bombs can free-fall or they can use a retarder system, meaning a parachute; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these solutions exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: FAB-100s and FAB-250s come in both versions, free-fall and retarded; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Air bombs were designed and tested for air-to-surface delivery and not surface-to-surface delivery; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let's talk about the rockets. The air bombs were modified by attaching rockets; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Different numbers or amounts of rockets were attached depending on the configurations of one rocket, three rockets, and four rockets; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The numbers of rocket motors FAB, but as for types, we found only one. From all that I've studied so far, they did not find any other rocket motor except Grad, G-r-a-d.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The first acronym in this answer was also Grad, not FAB.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could just finish with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your past testimony, at transcript page 38479, you were asked at line 19: "Q. We'll move on now to the characteristics of rockets. Now, I believe it is common ground that the air bombs were attached to different numbers of rockets depending on the configurations. And you have accepted that the air bombs were attached to rockets in configurations of one rocket, three rockets, and four rockets. Is that right?" Your answer was: "Yes, I analysed those types." Do you stand by that evidence? Excuse me, that testimony.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly. I stand by it. I just have to correct. It's not about different motors that were mounted on it. Those were only Grad motors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there was nothing in the question which suggested that the motors were any different. It was just about the number of motors, and you answered the question by saying "the number of rocket motors, but as for type," so you moved away from what was asked. We'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning. I give you the same instructions as I did before. You know them by heart now, I take it, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony. And you may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, where are we in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we did have a very productive conversation with counsel last week and I bring this up because it appears that we're going to be agreeable in terms of admitting investigative materials related to outstanding things. So with that in mind, I think I will finish within a less amount of time than counsel used on direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Less is perhaps beautiful, but how much less?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would have to look at the -- it will be around the same amount of time. I see based on what my current estimate is, is that I still have possibly close to two hours left so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So most likely you will finish in the first two sessions of tomorrow morning. That's two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we don't intervene too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We never object to any time our colleagues ask for their examination -- we never object to any extension of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the Chamber has some concerns. We are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's in your hands now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As we said yesterday, we are the guardians of expeditious proceedings, and that counts for both parties, and that it means inclusive the Prosecution. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 7th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of October, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
